candidates.name: National LIDAR Programme
verified_facts: England was divided into 302 survey blocks for Phase 1 national LiDAR capture.
Repeat surveys use incrementing phase numbers rather than implying a fixed rolling recapture.
Each 5km product tile name includes a survey id, OS grid reference, and survey-date range; an index catalogue supplies survey-specific information.
semantic_limits: Programme/block metadata identifies survey lineage; it does not by itself identify which composite survey supplied a parcel until matched through the catalogue.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Catalogues
verified_facts: The dataset is described as indices for full-coverage LiDAR surveys of England.
The catalogue record itself exposes no terrain data service or elevation raster resource.
semantic_limits: Catalogue records are lineage/index evidence only and cannot be sampled as elevation.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - GeoPackage spatial metadata index migration
verified_facts: LiDAR Composite and SurfZone download ZIPs now include a spatial metadata index in GeoPackage format.
The index describes the spatial location and temporal extent of raster elevation data.
Technical guides describe the index attribute schema.
semantic_limits: A metadata GeoPackage is not the elevation raster itself; it is used to establish spatial/temporal lineage.

candidates.name: Removal of Esri Image Services / persistent WCS endpoints
verified_facts: DSP replaced Esri image services with open-standard WCS and WMS services.
WMS is described as a summarised view while WCS provides elevation/raw pixel data.
Updated endpoint naming removes year suffixes so feeds can remain persistent across future updates.
semantic_limits: Persistent endpoint identity does not freeze source survey lineage; metadata must still be checked for the actual contributing survey.

candidates.name: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: Time-stamped DSM includes terrain plus vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
Tiles are GeoTIFFs aligned to the OS Grid and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The survey-specific metadata catalogue provides dates, resolution, transformation and geoid model.
semantic_limits: DSM is surface-object evidence and is excluded from primary bare-earth parcel height-difference calculations.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - downloading large areas
verified_facts: The open portal distributes LiDAR data in 5km by 5km tiles.
Several tiles can be downloaded together for relatively small areas; large-country supplies require offline handling.
semantic_limits: Download unit size is packaging only and must not be confused with raster resolution or survey footprint.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - ASCII to GeoTIFF migration
verified_facts: EA moved composite 1m/2m DTM delivery from ASCII to GeoTIFF.
GeoTIFF files are supplied in 5km tiles with elevations in metres.
The format migration enables efficient storage and web services such as WCS.
semantic_limits: A file-format migration does not improve the underlying elevation accuracy or change survey provenance.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - metadata and coverage for all LiDAR products
verified_facts: EA directs users to coverage maps/metadata to determine what LiDAR products exist at a location.
If no data is listed, the location has not been surveyed in the catalogue.
semantic_limits: Coverage existence is not proof that a specific survey contributed to a composite pixel until survey-index lineage is matched.

candidates.name: Adverse possession of historic/unregistered land (PG5) collection
verified_facts: PG5 applies to unregistered land and certain pre-13-October-2003 adverse-possession rights.
The collection was last updated 1 June 2026.
semantic_limits: Historic title procedure is legal evidence and does not establish terrain elevation.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry first registrations guidance
verified_facts: The guidance page groups first-registration, lost-deed and plan-preparation resources.
The guidance page was updated 16 June 2026.
semantic_limits: Guide currentness helps source selection but does not establish parcel geometry or elevation.

candidates.name: Practice guide 2: first registration where deeds are lost or destroyed
verified_facts: Updated 20 July 2026.
Where deeds are lost, title evidence must be reconstructed and HMLR can require an Ordnance Survey inspection.
If the property cannot be identified on the Ordnance Survey map, a suitable plan must be supplied.
semantic_limits: A reconstructed or inspection-supported registration plan is title evidence, not a terrain measurement surface.

candidates.name: Practice guide 1: first registrations
verified_facts: First registration may require a plan where postal description is insufficient.
Properties with different extents at different levels require enough information to define vertical and horizontal extents.
semantic_limits: Legal vertical extent in title registration is not the same concept as bare-earth elevation or LiDAR height difference.

candidates.name: Easements claimed by prescription (PG52)
verified_facts: Updated 1 June 2026.
The guide covers acquiring and registering easements claimed by prescription.
semantic_limits: An easement or right-of-way extent is an interest in land, not the canonical parcel polygon for terrain sampling.

candidates.name: Practice guide 57: exempting documents from inspection
verified_facts: Land Registration Act documents are generally open to inspection/copy subject to statutory exemptions.
The guide explains exempt-information document handling and official-copy access.
semantic_limits: Document access status is evidence availability metadata, not proof of exact boundary or elevation.

candidates.name: OGC API - Common - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: OGC API Common Part 1 is an approved OGC standard.
It defines shared landing-page, API-definition and conformance resources.
Implemented conformance classes are advertised through the /conformance resource.
semantic_limits: API conformance/discovery establishes service capabilities only; it does not validate terrain values.

candidates.name: OGC API - Features - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: OGC API Features Part 1 is an approved standard for feature discovery and retrieval.
Core feature geometries use the WGS84/CRS84 default conventions unless extensions are used.
Feature queries return selected features rather than coverage pixel values.
semantic_limits: Feature API geometry/metadata must not be treated as numeric terrain coverage.

candidates.name: OGC API - Features - Part 1: Core corrigendum
verified_facts: The corrigendum retains the Part 1 discovery/query scope and conformance classes.
It is a corrected revision of the approved Part 1 Core document.
semantic_limits: Implementation/version lineage must identify the applicable revision; corrigendum status does not change terrain-source accuracy.

candidates.name: CoverageJSON Community Standard
verified_facts: CoverageJSON is an OGC Community Standard for JSON-encoded spatiotemporal coverages.
A formal JSON schema is supplied to test conformance.
The standard is an encoding/representation contract.
semantic_limits: CoverageJSON conformance does not establish that an encoded elevation value is authoritative or parcel-specific.
